title: Very ample counterexamples to Kodaira vanishing on surfaces in every characteristic, answering a question of Raynaud
subject: math.AG
abstract: In 1978 Raynaud constructed a smooth projective surface in positive characteristic with an ample line bundle whose inverse has nonzero first cohomology, and asked whether Kodaira vanishing can also fail for an ample line bundle that is generated by its global sections, or even very ample. We answer both questions on surfaces, the smallest dimension in which they have content, and in every positive characteristic. On Raynaud's own surface in characteristic $2$ a modified twist $Q$ is ample and globally generated with $h^1(Q^{-1})=1$. Taking ninth roots of a general basis of the sections of $Q^{\otimes 9}$ then gives, over every algebraically closed field of characteristic $2$, a smooth projective surface $Y$ with a very ample line bundle $L$ such that $h^0(L)=562$, $h^1(L^{-1})=1$ and $h^1(\mathcal O_Y)=565$. The passage from globally generated to very ample is general: in any characteristic $p$, roots of degree prime to $p$ of a general basis turn a globally generated counterexample into a very ample one of the same dimension. In every characteristic $p$, a cyclic cover of degree $p+1$ of Tango's ruled surface carries an ample, globally generated $Q$ with $H^1(Q^{-1})\ne0$, so very ample counterexamples exist on surfaces in every positive characteristic. The earlier very ample counterexamples, on homogeneous spaces (Lauritzen) and on varieties of dimension at least six (Lauritzen and Rao), are not surfaces. On $Y$ the restriction of Picard schemes to a smooth curve of $|L|$ is not a closed immersion, which answers negatively the second part of a question of Kweon, in every characteristic. The mathematics was produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode) and checked by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high, which also wrote this text, and by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max. No human has checked it.
comments:
Version 3 adds Theorem 4, proved in a new Section 7: in every positive characteristic p there is a smooth projective surface with a very ample L such that H^1(L^{-1}) is nonzero, from a cyclic cover of degree p+1 of Tango's ruled surface over an Artin-Schreier curve. The characteristic-2 theorem (562, 1, 565), Theorem 3 and Corollary 2 are unchanged. Version 2 added Corollary 2 (the second part of Kweon's Question 7.7) and corrected Theorem 3. This note answers, for surfaces, the question M. Raynaud asked in Remarque 3 of his 1978 article (C. P. Ramanujam - a tribute, Tata Inst. Fund. Res. Studies in Math. 8, p. 278): whether Kodaira vanishing can fail for an ample line bundle generated by its sections, or even a very ample one. The characteristic-2 surface and the question are Raynaud's. The earlier very ample counterexamples, of N. Lauritzen and of N. Lauritzen and A. P. Rao, have dimension at least six. Covers by roots of sections are standard (B. Bhatt; S. Mukai); what is new is the globally generated twist on Raynaud's surface, its analogue on a cyclic cover of Tango's ruled surface in every characteristic, and the very ampleness of the root cover.

How it was produced. GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), in ChatGPT Pro mode, found the construction and its proofs in November 2026, in a research run on questions in algebraic geometry prompted by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) at effort max. Claude Opus 5.5, at effort high, wrote the present text on 23 November 2026 from the run's text: it separated the general theorem on roots of a basis from the example, wrote out the chart argument for the very ampleness of the ninth power, and replaced the run's ground field by an arbitrary algebraically closed field of characteristic 2, with Bertini's theorem.

How it was checked. All checks are of 23 November 2026. A separate instance of GPT-6 Astra reconstructed the geometry from the statement and the construction data alone, and two programs with different methods computed the dimensions 210, 186 and 160. Claude Opus 5.5, at effort high, checked every step and recomputed every invariant by hand. Claude Opus 5.5, at effort max, read the whole text, followed every step and recomputed every number. Raynaud's article (pp. 273-278) was read at the source, with the opening pages of the articles of Lauritzen and Rao, Mukai and Ekedahl and the cited statements of Bernasconi and Valloni. Two web searches and a search of Hexagon on 23 November 2026 found no very ample counterexample on a surface. No human has checked the proof or the text, and nothing is formalized.

Version 3. The construction in every characteristic (Theorem 4) was produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode) in a separate research run on crystalline questions in positive characteristic. Claude Opus 5.5, at effort max, made a targeted check of its vanishing ranges. Claude Opus 5.5, at effort high, checked every step and every invariant against that run's text for every prime p, and wrote Section 7. Claude Opus 5.5, at effort max, read Section 7 step by step and every page of version 3 before posting. No human has checked it.
